reasoning: Both attempts correctly move the selection into a private Charm signal, keep validation in setBlockType, remove BlockTypeChanged, and update the ghost color through Charm. B calls useSignalState in app() inside mount and passes a plain Vide source to an unchanged BlockPicker. A puts the vide-charm bridge inside BlockPicker, which ties the view to Charm and silently changes what the Selected prop means: a Vide source would stop updating. A also renames the public getter for no reason. B is the cleaner change that a developer would merge.

criteria.criterion: BlockPlacer owns selection as Charm signal
criteria.note: `local getSelectedName, setSelectedName = Charm.signal(...)`, only the getter is exported as `selectedBlockType`, and `setBlockType` still asserts `BlockTypes.ByName[name]`.

criteria.criterion: Hotbar bridges Charm into Vide state inside mounted scope
criteria.note: `useSignalState(props.Selected)` in the `blockPicker` body runs inside `mount` through `app()`, so it is tracked and disposed correctly, but the bridge sits in the view, not the caller.

criteria.criterion: Single copy of selection, BlockTypeChanged removed
criteria.note: The mirrored `source` and the BindableEvent are both removed, and the check confirms no file mentions BlockTypeChanged.
`Charm.effect(function() applyBlockType(BlockPlacer.selectedBlockType()) end)` runs once now and again on every change.
BlockPicker now requires VideCharm and wraps `props.Selected` with `useSignalState`, so the prop must be a Charm getter, and a Vide source passed by a caller or story would never update.
Works and passes all checks, but it renames `getBlockType` to `selectedBlockType`, which is more API churn than needed.

criteria.note: `VideCharm.useSignalState(BlockPlacer.getBlockType)` sits in the `app()` body passed to `mount`, so the state is tracked and disposed with the UI.

criteria.criterion: Single copy of selection, BlockTypeChanged removed
criteria.note: The mirror source, its Connect, and the BindableEvent are removed, so only the Charm signal remains.
`Charm.listen(BlockPlacer.getBlockType, applyBlockType)` applies the color right away and on every change.
